text:
elaine: Heads up 1 - we've started bring-up for Lattice-10B-econ (QAT 4-bit) for a cost-sensitive chat tier. Before any customer routing: legal check on hosting, attribution, and an odd "patent grant" clause in their repo.

mark: quick perf note 1 - QAT 4-bit reduces token cost x3, p95 latency ~2.9x lower. Eval: small regressions on multi-step planning (-3.1%), embeddings quality for duplicates -1.8%.

elaine: pasted the license excerpt below. main concern: clause 4 mentions "no inference-as-a-service" and clause 7 references a limited patent license that might have an export control caveat.

ci-bot: ```
LATTICE RESEARCH LICENSE v1.1
1. Permitted: research and evaluation for non-commercial purposes.
2. Redistribution: distribution of model weights or derivative binaries is prohibited without explicit written permission.
3. Attribution: Derivative Works must include a visible attribution and link to the license.
4. Service restriction: providing the Modelor any Derivativeas an online inference service to paying users is prohibited unless a commercial license is obtained.
5. Patent grant: contributors grant a limited, revocable patent license for research use only; commercial exploitation requires a separate patent sublicense.
6. Export controls: subject to applicable export laws; downstream commercial hosts must ensure compliance.
7. Transformations: quantization/compression are deemed Derivative Works unless waived.
```

olga (legal): short take 1 - two blockers: (A) service restriction blocks our hosted paid API; (B) patent grant + export-control language means we need to be careful re: customers in restricted jurisdictions and any indemnity ask. Attribution is straightforward.

dave: clarifying question 1 - we're not distributing binary blobs externally, we only persist encrypted quant shards internally and serve in-memory. Could that still be considered providing inference-as-a-service?

olga (legal): yes. The license explicitly calls out "providing the Model or any Derivative as an online inference service". Even if shards stay internal, offering outputs to paying users counts.

mark: product-wise we can (A) keep QAT builds strictly internal for benchmark/canary, (B) enable Private/BYO where customer uploads their own Lattice binary into a VPC, or (C) request a commercial license and patent sublicense from Lattice Research.

elaine: UI attribution Q: they'd like a "visible attribution". Is a model card + endpoint metadata enough, or do we need something more prominent in our hosted app?

olga (legal): model card + an explicit line in Console where model is selected should satisfy "visible" in most cases. Also add the license page link in the endpoint documentation and TOS. We'll propose a sample string in outreach.

ci-bot: policy reminder: set onboarding 'legal' = pending and mark 'hosted:blocked'.

mark: outreach draft notes for engineering: include exact quant method (QAT 4-bit per-channel symmetric), training delta summary, that we will not publish quant binaries without permission, store shards encrypted, and can enforce geo-checks for export controls. Also offer to include attribution string and a telemetry snippet they can review.

olga (legal): outreach asks we should make: 1) confirmation that in-memory serving of our quantized runtime is considered Derivative/hosting; 2) request a commercial hosting + patent sublicense; 3) acceptable attribution text and placement; 4) export control checklist and permitted geos; 5) whether they'd accept a revenue-share or fee.

elaine: engineering action items 1 - attach perf CSV, commit hash, quant pipeline doc, and a short note on geo-blocking and KMS usage. We'll keep the model flagged "research-only" in catalog.

mark: quick mitigation if they refuse: enable a BYO path for Dedicated (customer supplies binary in their VPC) and recommend our Private deployment. For Dedicated-managed we block until cleared.

olga (legal): also note: if they grant hosting but require patent sublicense, that can take longer (legal negotiation). Prepare to propose a limited-term pilot license for initial customers to shorten timeline.

ci-bot: action recorded: tag onboarding entry 'legal:pending', 'hosted:block', and schedule legal+eng sync next Tue.

dave: I'll draft the technical appendix and include the shard encryption details, fallback-to-FP16 policy, and the canary thresholds.

elaine: thanks team. Once olga has outreach language we'll send and keep this thread updated. Leaving thread open for any urgent sales asks. :wave:
